decision: Keep the runtime frontend fail-closed. Audit reuse of nv_system_pm_lock and a dedicated lifecycle gate; include PCI removal, deferred work, partial MSI-X registration, UVM work, failure rollback, and lock ordering before implementing any live drain.

observations.finding: The documented order is nv_linux_devices_lock, then nvl->ldata_lock; release the list lock before releasing ldata_lock.

The provider holds nv_linux_devices_lock while calling nv_preempt_user_channels(); that wrapper takes and releases ldata_lock around RM stop, so ldata_lock is not retained by the provider after the stop returns.
Legacy/MSI or MSI-X IRQs are requested during nv_start_device before NV_FLAG_OPEN is set. Persistent-state and SoC paths differ. The flag alone cannot identify a fully registered IRQ set.
Close enters nv_linux_state through ldata_lock and the last close can stop the device; adapter shutdown stops bottom_half_q, frees legacy/MSI or MSI-X IRQs, and releases the MSI-X array.

The inspected PCI remove callback takes device-list and ldata locks and can shut down/free the adapter, but it does not acquire nv_system_pm_lock. That existing rwsem therefore does not by itself pin the complete nvl/IRQ lifetime against remove.
The ISR can queue bottom_half_q work separately from the IRQ thread. synchronize_irq() alone does not flush this driver queue; shutdown stops it, but that is not a pre-UVM drain contract.
The common frontend drain callback currently returns -EOPNOTSUPP for either backend. Therefore the coordinator rolls channels back and returns before shared UVM suspend.

The existing nv_system_pm_lock read side covers ordinary GPU open/close and many control operations; its write side is used by the separate procfs power-state path. Hybrid provider PM APIs do not currently acquire it, and PCI remove is outside it. UVM work coverage and cross-backend ordering remain under audit.

synchronize_irq() waits current IRQ handlers but does not disable future interrupts; holding a resource required by an IRQ callback while waiting can deadlock. This cannot alone prove a no-new-fault boundary or drain the separate NVIDIA bottom-half queue.
